Year's coldest month (-33°C nights) with the pass completely snowbound. No civilian access. Road clearance by BRO is months away.

who_should_avoid: Early-month visitors; civilian traffic still blocked
why_not: BRO begins clearance operations but the pass remains closed to civilian traffic (-25°C nights). Early access attempts will fail.

who_should_avoid: Those unable to handle road closure or expect sudden reopening
why_not: BRO clearance is underway but civilian passage remains officially closed (-18°C nights). Apricot blossoms appear in lower Nubra but the pass itself is inaccessible.

things_to_do: Cross Khardung La in late month when roads clear
Trek or drive Nubra valley circuits with apricot blossom tail
Acclimatise 48 hours in Leh before attempting 5,359m
why_go: May brings late-spring opening (-10 to 5°C) when the pass opens late month. ILP permits are fast-tracked. The Nubra circuit opens at full operation. Apricot blossoms tail into Nubra. This is the entry gate to the high-altitude season.
why_not: Unpredictable late-month closures due to snow and avalanche risk mean you could drive 5+ hours from Leh only to find the pass shut. Plan flexibility.

things_to_do: Cross Khardung La with clear 5,359m views
Explore Nubra valley circuits at full operation
Trek to Diskit Monastery and surrounding valleys
why_go: June is peak season (-5 to 10°C) with the pass open reliably. ILP fast-tracked. Nubra circuit at full operation. Apricot fruit on trees. This is the entry month for confident pass-crossers with solid acclimatisation.
pack_list: Hat, gloves, thermal socks, sunscreen SPF 50+

things_to_do: Cross Khardung La en route to Nubra circuits
Trek and explore Diskit, Sumur, and Panamik valleys
Photograph apricot harvest in full swing
why_go: July is peak (-3 to 12°C) with continued clear conditions. Apricot harvest is active across Nubra. ILP processing remains fast. Nubra hotels are tight but operational. The pass is fully open and reliable.

things_to_do: Cross Khardung La in late summer conditions
Explore Nubra circuits with apricot harvest tail
Visit Diskit Monastery and surrounding valleys
why_go: August is peak season (-3 to 12°C) with the pass fully open. Independence Day weekend tightens accommodation. Apricot harvest concludes. ILP processing is streamlined. This remains one of the best months for Khardung La crossing.

things_to_do: Cross Khardung La in year's best clarity
Attend Ladakh Festival (early September)
Explore Nubra circuits in dry, clear conditions
why_go: September is year's best (-7 to 10°C, dry, clear). The pass is fully open and reliable. Ladakh Festival (early Sep) creates festive energy. Last solid month before October's weather deterioration. Clarity is maximal for photography.

things_to_do: Cross Khardung La early month before closures begin
Explore Nubra circuits while weather holds
Drive pass at dawn for clearest conditions
why_go: October is late season (-15 to 5°C) with clear skies but increasing early-month risk of mid-month snow closure. Manali-Leh highway shuts. Nubra circuits narrow operations. Timing is critical: early month is safe; mid-late month is unpredictable.
why_not: Early snowfall unpredictably closes the pass mid-month, stranding vehicles for 24–72 hours. Plan accordingly or consider waiting for November.
The pass closes for winter mid-November (-20°C nights) as snow accumulation makes civilian passage impassable. Road remains closed until May. Plan all Ladakh/Nubra travel for June-October window.
The pass is closed to civilian traffic (-28°C nights) under deep winter snow. Road is inaccessible for 5+ months (December–April). Only mountaineers reach this altitude in winter.

things_to_do: Trek Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary trails (20 sq km)
Explore terraced rice paddies in post-harvest state
Visit traditional Angami stone houses and view the 700-year village history
why_go: January brings cool (4–16°C), crisp, dry conditions ideal for trekking the conservation sanctuary. The rice paddies are clear of crops; stone architecture and village layouts are fully visible. The village's sustainable conservation model is the primary draw.

things_to_do: Trek the Tragopan Sanctuary in clear, dry conditions
Photograph Angami stone architecture and village layout
Explore the conservation model and community-run initiatives
why_go: February is late winter (6–18°C), fully dry, and comfortable for extended hikes through the sanctuary. The 700-year Angami warrior legacy is best understood in clear, quiet conditions. This is peak season clarity.

things_to_do: Trek the sanctuary as flowers bloom
Photograph spring bird activity in the protected forest
Explore village terraces and historic architecture
why_go: March brings spring (10–22°C) with flowers blooming across the sanctuary. Bird activity peaks pre-monsoon. Trails are dry and well-maintained. This is an optimal spring trekking month.

who_should_avoid: Those unable to tolerate muddy monsoon onset
things_to_do: Early-morning sanctuary trek before rain begins
why_not: Late spring (14–26°C) sees pre-monsoon showers arriving. Trails become muddy and visibility unpredictable. The rainforest trails that make Khonoma special turn into mud challenges.

Pre-monsoon rains (16–28°C) make forest trails muddy and leech-prone. The primary appeal — trekking through the protected sanctuary — becomes uncomfortable. Visibility and trail conditions deteriorate sharply.

who_should_avoid: Trekkers dependent on clear, dry trails
why_not: Monsoon (18–28°C, heavy rain) makes trails dangerously slippery. Leeches are abundant. Visibility collapses. The sanctuary's beauty is obscured by clouds and downpours.

who_should_avoid: All trekkers seeking good trail conditions
why_not: Peak monsoon (18–27°C, continuous rain) makes forest trekking miserable. Leeches thrive. Trails are waterlogged. Visibility is near-zero in the dense forest.
Late monsoon (18–27°C, heavy rain) leaves trails waterlogged and leech-infested. The Khonoma experience — forest trekking and terrace photography — is severely compromised.

who_should_avoid: Those unable to handle frequent residual showers
things_to_do: Early-month visits only as rain tapers late-month
why_not: Early September (16–26°C) sees frequent showers that obscure the rice terraces you came to photograph. Trails remain muddy from retreating monsoon. Late-month visits are better.

things_to_do: Trek Tragopan Sanctuary in clear autumn weather
Photograph rice terraces and stone houses
Explore the conservation sanctuary and wildlife viewing paths
why_go: October is autumn (12–24°C), dry and clear. Post-monsoon verdancy peaks. Trails are fully dry. Photography conditions are excellent — the combination of terraced fields, stone architecture, and protected sanctuary at green-maximum is compelling.
pack_list: Light layers for variable autumn temps

things_to_do: Extended multi-hour treks through the sanctuary
Document the village's sustainable conservation model
Photograph terraced fields and Angami architecture in perfect weather
why_go: November is early winter (6–20°C) with perfect trekking weather. Trails are dry and clear. Visibility is optimal. This is the peak month for experiencing Khonoma's unique combination of forest sanctuary, terraced agriculture, and living Angami culture.

things_to_do: Trek Tragopan Sanctuary in cool, clear conditions
Explore the village and its 700-year history
Photograph Angami stone houses and terraced landscape
why_go: December is winter (4–18°C), cool and dry, with excellent trail conditions and visibility. Year-end holidays bring explorers seeking authentic cultural experiences. The combination of trekking, cultural immersion, and conservation model study makes this a compelling month.
pack_list: Hat, gloves (for very early morning starts), sunscreen

things_to_do: Early morning cave visit only, depart by 9am
why_not: April pre-monsoon heat (22–32°C, 75% humidity) makes the 3km exposed walking route between caves exhausting. Afternoon visits are uncomfortable and risk heat exhaustion.
